name: Face-Reconstructed Gauss Smoothing
definition: A second point-data field storing a face-reconstructed value obtained from the voxel value, six neighbor-averaged face values, and two-point Gauss quadrature inside each voxel.
summary: Face-Reconstructed Gauss Smoothing reduces discretization artifacts in voxelized fields by reconstructing a continuous quadratic polynomial from center and face values, then sampling it at Gauss quadrature points.
